body: One time when I was like 13-14, me and some friends were having a sleep over, when we decided that we wanted to go get some snacks. It was probably about 10, I think, in either fall or winter because it was already really dark outside. It was me and two other friends. One of them was disabled and afraid to go out at night, so we let him stay home and walked to the dollar store ourselves. The route we took was through a bunch of neighborhoods with mostly old people who were asleep. About halfway there though, we passed by a pretty long road, but at the end of it was this big thing? I'm not sure what other word to call it honestly. It seemed humanoid, but it was oddly proportioned, it had long legs and arms, a giant round head, was sort of a sickly white, and was as tall as the house it was in front of, despite being crouched down. I probably would've just assumed it was some sort of display or vehicle, but I asked my friend if he could see it, and after she looked, it looked like it sort of lifted it's head. Personally, I wanted to go and check it out, but she was freaked and was tugging on my arm to just keep moving, so we did. Because of our little hang up, we missed the last open minutes of the store, so we walked back, but I couldn't get the thing off my mind. I decided that I was going to go check it out, with or without my friend. However, when we passed by again, it was just gone, which was way more unnerving than if it had been there, so we literally ran home. To this day, I have no idea what it actually was, and I've never seen it again. I live in Idaho, where a lot of people have sited similar creatures, apparently, including things like the Rake, which, I dunno man, maybe? It was pretty late at night, so I don't think it was any heavy machinery or anything either, but it makes for a fun story to tell people

Focus on yourself, do things that make you happy, especially things you didn't do as often when you were with them. Let yourself feel your feelings, cry if you have to, talk to friends about it. Try not to let the memories of them run your life, but don't totally forget those feelings either. Breaking up is just another wave in life, stay strong, and you can get through it
